attestations.text: WU Hsi-ch'i 吴錫麒 (T. 聖徵, H. 穀人), 1746–1818, man of letters, was a native of Ch'ien-t'ang (Hangchow). A chin-shih of 1775, he first was appointed a sub-reader in the Hanlin Academy. After having passed through several positions, including that of second-class compiler, he finally became a libationer.
